document_title: Anyone can ride Waymo to the San Antonio airport now. The flood fix is still listed in development
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
A car with no driver now goes to San Antonio International.

From October 14th anyone with the Waymo app can hail one in San Antonio, the airport included. Airports director Jesus Saenz said travelers now have "a new option to get there."

It is the same service that paused after the April flooding. Texas Public Radio reported an empty Waymo washed into Salado Creek in heavy rain on April 20th. Nobody was hurt.

The federal recall record says the software "may allow the vehicle to slow and then drive into standing water on higher speed roadways." It lists 3,791 potentially affected units.

Read on October 16th, the record still lists the remedy as under development. Waymo's interim step was tighter weather limits and updated maps. NHTSA's recall lookup carries the remedy field under Waymo LLC. What will the finished remedy change at the water's edge?

S1.headline: Anyone can ride one to the airport now
S1.body: On October 14th Waymo opened its San Antonio robotaxis to anyone with the app, San Antonio International Airport included. The federal record of its flood recall still lists the remedy as under development. Drawn to illustrate.
strings: Anyone can ride one to the airport now

On October 14th Waymo opened its San Antonio robotaxis to anyone with the app, San Antonio International Airport included. The federal record of its flood recall still lists the remedy as under development. Drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: In February, it came by invitation
S2.body: Waymo took its first public riders in San Antonio on February 24th, inviting them from the tens of thousands across four cities who had the app. Texas Public Radio put that first service area at 60 square miles. Drawn to illustrate.

S3.headline: April 20th, Salado Creek
S3.body: Texas Public Radio reported an empty Waymo was swept up in flood waters and washed into the creek during heavy rain, and that no one was hurt. Earlier that April another was stranded in floodwater near McCullough Avenue and Contour Drive. Drawn to illustrate.
strings: Texas Public Radio reported an empty Waymo was swept up in flood waters and washed into the creek during heavy rain, and that no one was hurt. Earlier that April another was stranded in floodwater near McCullough Avenue and Contour Drive. Drawn to illustrate.

S4.headline: It slowed. Then it drove in
S4.body: The recall record says the software may let the vehicle slow and then drive into standing water on higher speed roadways. Texas Public Radio reports the notice said it detected the flooded road and kept going. The report reached regulators 11 days after the creek. Drawn to illustrate.
strings: It slowed. Then it drove in

S5.kicker: The recall, by its own count
S5.headline: 3,791 of them
S5.body: The recall covers 5th and 6th generation automated driving systems, 3,791 potentially affected units by the federal record's count. One is drawn here for each. Drawn to illustrate.
strings: The recall covers 5th and 6th generation automated driving systems, 3,791 potentially affected units by the federal record's count. One is drawn here for each. Drawn to illustrate.
The recall, by its own count

S6.headline: The cars ran without riders
S6.body: Texas Public Radio called the flood pause Waymo's longest in San Antonio to date. In May its cars ran in the city without serving riders while it reviewed its flood procedures. Drawn to illustrate.
strings: Texas Public Radio called the flood pause Waymo's longest in San Antonio to date. In May its cars ran in the city without serving riders while it reviewed its flood procedures. Drawn to illustrate.

S7.kicker: One post a day, February 24th to October 14th
S7.headline: 177 days from the creek to the curb
S7.body: One post for each day from February 24th to October 14th, a row for each month. The blue band is April 20th. The posts lit after it count the days until anyone could ride.

S8.headline: "The remedy is currently under development"
S8.body: That is the federal recall record's remedy field as read on October 16th. In the meantime Waymo tightened its weather limits and updated its maps. Every affected vehicle had that interim update by April 20th.
strings: That is the federal recall record's remedy field as read on October 16th. In the meantime Waymo tightened its weather limits and updated its maps. Every affected vehicle had that interim update by April 20th.
The remedy is currently under development.

S9.headline: Open to anyone. The fix is still listed in development
S9.body: The airport called the rides a new option to get there. The recall's remedy field is public, and anyone can read it on NHTSA's recall lookup under Waymo LLC. Drawn to illustrate.
